info.title: Meraki Dashboard API
info.description:
A RESTful API to programmatically manage and monitor Cisco Meraki networks at scale.

> Date: 02 September, 2026
>
> [Recent Updates](https://meraki.io/whats-new/)

---

[API Documentation](https://meraki.io/api)

[Community Support](https://meraki.io/community)

[Meraki Homepage](https://www.meraki.com)

post.description: Create a synchronous AI assistant chat completion for user-wide threads. If 'threadId' is omitted, the request is handled as a one-off invocation and no reusable thread is created. For durable multi-turn conversations or richer media support (audio, files), create a thread and use the messages endpoint.

query.description: Simple text question or instruction to send to the AI assistant. Provide either 'query' for text-only requests or 'content' for multi-modal input.

text.description: Text content. Required when type is 'text'.

mediaType.description: Image MIME type. SVG and other executable content types are not accepted.

source.description: Base64-encoded media source. Required when type is 'image'.

content.description: List of multi-modal content blocks. Use instead of 'query' to send text or images. Supports text and image types only; for audio and file support, use the messages endpoint. Maximum 8 parts.

threadId.description: Existing persisted thread ID to continue synchronously. If omitted, the request is handled as a one-off invocation and the response will not include a reusable thread ID.

platform.description: Platform identifier. Defaults to MERAKI when omitted. Case-insensitive.

language.description: Optional language override. Defaults to the user's preferred language.

country.description: Optional country override. Defaults to the user's country.

example.query: What is the uplink status for my MX appliances?

content.text: What is the uplink status for my MX appliances?

threadId.description: Reusable thread ID returned when the completion continues an existing persisted thread. Omitted for one-off completions.

messageId.description: Persisted assistant message ID when one was created. Null for one-off completions.

sources.description: References or data sources used to generate the response

example.content: A dormant device is a device that has not been active for a period of time

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 1000. Default is 1000.

parameters.name: startingAfter
parameters.description: A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.

get.description: Returns a historical log of all commands

parameters.name: serial
parameters.description: Serial

parameters.name: operations
parameters.description: Optional parameter to filter commands by operation. Allowed values are disableDownstreamPower, enableDownstreamPower, cycleDownstreamPower, and refreshData.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 1000. Default is 10.

parameters.name: startingAfter
parameters.description: A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.

parameters.name: endingBefore
parameters.description: A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.

parameters.name: sortOrder
parameters.description: Sorted order of entries. Order options are 'ascending' and 'descending'. Default is 'descending'.

parameters.name: t0
parameters.description: The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 30 days from today.

parameters.name: t1
parameters.description: The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 30 days after t0.

parameters.name: timespan
parameters.description: The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 30 days. The default is 30 days.

parameters.name: networkId
parameters.description: Network ID

defaultRulesEnabled.description: Whether default traffic shaping rules are enabled (true) or disabled (false). There are 4 default rules, which can be seen on your network's traffic shaping page. Note that default rules count against the rule limit of 8.

type.description: The type of definition. Can be one of 'application', 'applicationCategory', 'host', 'port', 'ipRange' or 'localNet'.

value.description:
If "type" is 'host', 'port', 'ipRange' or 'localNet', then "value" must be a string, matching either
    a hostname (e.g. "somesite.com"), a port (e.g. 8080), or an IP range ("192.1.0.0",
    "192.1.0.0/16", or "10.1.0.0/16:80"). 'localNet' also supports CIDR notation, excluding
    custom ports.
     If "type" is 'application' or 'applicationCategory', then "value" must be an object
    with the structure { "id": "meraki:layer7/..." }, where "id" is the application category or
    application ID (for a list of IDs for your network, use the trafficShaping/applicationCategories
    endpoint).

definitions.description: A list of objects describing the definitions of your traffic shaping rule. At least one definition is required.

settings.description: How bandwidth limits are applied by your rule. Can be one of 'network default', 'ignore' or 'custom'.

limitUp.description: The maximum upload limit (integer, in Kbps).

limitDown.description: The maximum download limit (integer, in Kbps).

bandwidthLimits.description: The bandwidth limits object, specifying the upload ('limitUp') and download ('limitDown') speed in Kbps. These are only enforced if 'settings' is set to 'custom'.

perClientBandwidthLimits.description: An object describing the bandwidth settings for your rule.

dscpTagValue.description:
The DSCP tag applied by your rule. null means 'Do not change DSCP tag'.
    For a list of possible tag values, use the trafficShaping/dscpTaggingOptions endpoint.

priority.description:
A string, indicating the priority level for packets bound to your rule.
    Can be 'low', 'normal' or 'high'.

rules.description:
An array of traffic shaping rules. Rules are applied in the order that
    they are specified in. An empty list (or null) means no rules. Note that
    you are allowed a maximum of 8 rules.

get.description: List the events for the network

parameters.name: networkId
parameters.description: Network ID

parameters.name: productType
parameters.description: The product type to fetch events for. This parameter is required for networks with multiple device types. Valid types are wireless, appliance, switch, systemsManager, camera, cellularGateway, wirelessController, campusGateway, and secureConnect

parameters.name: includedEventTypes
parameters.description: A list of event types. The returned events will be filtered to only include events with these types.

parameters.name: excludedEventTypes
parameters.description: A list of event types. The returned events will be filtered to exclude events with these types.

parameters.name: deviceMac
parameters.description: The MAC address of the Meraki device which the list of events will be filtered with

parameters.name: deviceSerial
parameters.description: The serial of the Meraki device which the list of events will be filtered with

parameters.name: deviceName
parameters.description: The name of the Meraki device which the list of events will be filtered with

parameters.name: clientIp
parameters.description: The IP of the client which the list of events will be filtered with. Only supported for track-by-IP networks.

parameters.name: clientMac
parameters.description: The MAC address of the client which the list of events will be filtered with. Only supported for track-by-MAC networks.

parameters.name: clientName
parameters.description: The name, or partial name, of the client which the list of events will be filtered with

parameters.name: smDeviceMac
parameters.description: The MAC address of the Systems Manager device which the list of events will be filtered with

parameters.name: smDeviceName
parameters.description: The name of the Systems Manager device which the list of events will be filtered with

parameters.name: eventDetails
parameters.description: The details of the event(Catalyst device only) which the list of events will be filtered with

parameters.name: eventSeverity
parameters.description: The severity of the event(Catalyst device only) which the list of events will be filtered with

parameters.name: isCatalyst
parameters.description: Boolean indicating that whether it is a Catalyst device. For Catalyst device, eventDetails and eventSeverity can be used to filter events.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 1000. Default is 10.

parameters.name: startingAfter
parameters.description: A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.

parameters.name: endingBefore
parameters.description: A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.

message.description: A message regarding the events sent. Usually 'null' unless there are no events

pageStartAt.description: An UTC ISO8601 string of the earliest occured at time of the listed events of the page.

pageEndAt.description: An UTC ISO8601 string of the latest occured at time of the listed events of the page.

occurredAt.description: An UTC ISO8601 string of the time the event occurred at.

type.description: The type of event being listed.

description.description: A description of the event the happened.

category.description: The category that the event type belongs to

clientId.description: A string identifying the client. This could be a client's MAC or IP address

clientDescription.description: A description of the client. This is usually the client's device name.

deviceSerial.description: The serial number of the device. Only shown if the device is an access point.

deviceName.description: The name of the device. Only shown if the device is an access point.

ssidNumber.description: The SSID number of the device.

radio.description: The radio band number the client is trying to connect to.

vap.description: The virtual access point (VAP) number the client is connecting to.

channel.description: The radio channel the client is connecting to.

rssi.description: The current received signal strength indication (RSSI) of the client connected to an AP.

aid.description: The association ID of the client.

eventData.description: An object containing more data related to the event.

events.description: An array of events that took place in the network.

example.message: Some error

Link.description: A comma-separated list of first, last, prev, and next relative links used for subsequent paginated requests.

parameters.description: The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 31 days. The default is 7 days.

parameters.description: Filter results by AP tag; either :clientId or :deviceSerial must be jointly specified.

parameters.description: Filter results by SSID number.

radiusOverride.description: If true, the RADIUS response can override VLAN tag. This is not valid when ipAssignmentMode is 'NAT mode'. Only present when the SSID uses RADIUS-based auth and the network supports group policies.

adultContentFilteringEnabled.description: Boolean indicating whether or not adult content will be blocked. Only present when ipAssignmentMode is 'NAT mode'.

enabled.description: Boolean indicating whether or not DNS server rewrite is enabled. If disabled, upstream DNS will be used.

dnsCustomNameservers.description: User specified DNS servers (up to two servers)

dnsRewrite.description: DNS servers rewrite settings. Only present when ipAssignmentMode is 'NAT mode'.

gre.description: Ethernet over GRE settings. Only present when ipAssignmentMode is 'Ethernet over GRE'.

put.description: Update the traffic shaping rules for an SSID on an MR network.

parameters.name: networkId
parameters.description: Network ID

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Number

trafficShapingEnabled.description: Whether traffic shaping rules are applied to clients on your SSID.

defaultRulesEnabled.description: Whether default traffic shaping rules are enabled (true) or disabled (false). There are 4 default rules, which can be seen on your network's traffic shaping page. Note that default rules count against the rule limit of 8.

type.description: The type of definition. Can be one of 'application', 'applicationCategory', 'host', 'port', 'ipRange' or 'localNet'.

value.description:
If "type" is 'host', 'port', 'ipRange' or 'localNet', then "value" must be a string, matching either
    a hostname (e.g. "somesite.com"), a port (e.g. 8080), or an IP range ("192.1.0.0",
    "192.1.0.0/16", or "10.1.0.0/16:80"). 'localNet' also supports CIDR notation, excluding
    custom ports.
     If "type" is 'application' or 'applicationCategory', then "value" must be an object
    with the structure { "id": "meraki:layer7/..." }, where "id" is the application category or
    application ID (for a list of IDs for your network, use the trafficShaping/applicationCategories
    endpoint).

definitions.description: A list of objects describing the definitions of your traffic shaping rule. At least one definition is required.

settings.description: How bandwidth limits are applied by your rule. Can be one of 'network default', 'ignore' or 'custom'.

limitUp.description: The maximum upload limit (integer, in Kbps).

limitDown.description: The maximum download limit (integer, in Kbps).

bandwidthLimits.description: The bandwidth limits object, specifying the upload ('limitUp') and download ('limitDown') speed in Kbps. These are only enforced if 'settings' is set to 'custom'.

perClientBandwidthLimits.description: An object describing the bandwidth settings for your rule.

dscpTagValue.description:
The DSCP tag applied by your rule. null means 'Do not change DSCP tag'.
    For a list of possible tag values, use the trafficShaping/dscpTaggingOptions endpoint.

pcpTagValue.description:
The PCP tag applied by your rule. Can be 0 (lowest priority) through 7 (highest priority).
    null means 'Do not set PCP tag'.

rules.description:
An array of traffic shaping rules. Rules are applied in the order that
    they are specified in. An empty list (or null) means no rules. Note that
    you are allowed a maximum of 8 rules.

parameters.description: The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 31 days from today.

parameters.name: t1
parameters.description: The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 31 days after t0.

parameters.name: timespan
parameters.description: The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 31 days. The default is 7 days.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: The time resolution in seconds for returned data. The valid resolutions are: 300, 600, 1200, 3600, 14400, 86400. The default is 86400.

parameters.name: autoResolution
parameters.description: Automatically select a data resolution based on the given timespan; this overrides the value specified by the 'resolution' parameter. The default setting is false.

parameters.name: clientId
parameters.description: Filter results by network client to return per-device AP usage over time inner joined by the queried client's connection history.

parameters.name: deviceSerial
parameters.description: Filter results by device. Requires :band.

parameters.name: apTag
parameters.description: Filter results by AP tag; either :clientId or :deviceSerial must be jointly specified.

parameters.name: band
parameters.description: Filter results by band (either '2.4', '5' or '6').

parameters.name: ssid
parameters.description: Filter results by SSID number.

get.description: List shared MX port RADIUS servers by network. Each returned item is the network grouping itself, identified by networkId and name, with servers containing that network's shared RADIUS servers. These servers are shared by all MX ports in the network using '802.1X', 'MAC RADIUS' (MAC-based RADIUS authentication), or 'hybrid' (802.1X authentication with MAC-based RADIUS fallback) access policies. The endpoint pages networks first, then loads RADIUS servers for that page with a single server lookup scoped by network IDs, supported server types, and optional serverIds. Focused Rails controller benchmarking of the documented maximum page shape, 100 networks with 300 total server objects, measured p99 0.8199 seconds across 8 runs. This beta operation is available only to organizations with beta API access and may change before GA.

localId.description: [optional] The local ID is used to identify the MX to the peer. This will apply to all MXs this peer applies to.

secret.description: The shared secret with the VPN peer

ikeCipherAlgo.description: This is the cipher algorithm to be used in Phase 1. The value should be an array with one of the following algorithms: 'aes256', 'aes192', 'aes128', 'tripledes', 'des'

ikeAuthAlgo.description: This is the authentication algorithm to be used in Phase 1. The value should be an array with one of the following algorithms: 'sha256', 'sha1', 'md5'

ikeDiffieHellmanGroup.description: This is the Diffie-Hellman group to be used in Phase 1. The value should be an array with one of the following algorithms: 'group14', 'group5', 'group2', 'group1'

ikeLifetime.description: The lifetime of the Phase 1 SA in seconds.

childCipherAlgo.description: This is the cipher algorithms to be used in Phase 2. The value should be an array with one or more of the following algorithms: 'aes256', 'aes192', 'aes128', 'tripledes', 'des', 'null'

childAuthAlgo.description: This is the authentication algorithms to be used in Phase 2. The value should be an array with one of the following algorithms: 'sha256', 'sha1', 'md5'

childPfsGroup.description: This is the Diffie-Hellman group to be used for Perfect Forward Secrecy in Phase 2. The value should be an array with one of the following values: 'disabled','group14', 'group5', 'group2', 'group1'

childLifetime.description: The lifetime of the Phase 2 SA in seconds.

ipsecPolicies.description: Custom IPSec policies for the VPN peer. If not included and a preset has not been chosen, the default preset for IPSec policies will be used.

id.description: The ID of the SLA policy

slaPolicy.description: [optional] Information about the SLA policy to be applied to the peer

ipsecPoliciesPreset.description: One of the following available presets: 'default', 'aws', 'azure', 'umbrella', 'umbrella_short_lived', 'secure', 'zscaler'. If this is provided, the 'ipsecPolicies' parameter is ignored. Note that 'umbrella_short_lived' maps to the Dashboard UI label 'Umbrella', while 'umbrella' maps to the Dashboard UI label 'Umbrella (Deprecated)'.

ikeVersion.description: [optional] The IKE version to be used for the IPsec VPN peer configuration. Defaults to '1' when omitted.

networkTags.description: A list of network tags that will connect with this peer. Use ['all'] for all networks. Use ['none'] for no networks. If not included, the default is ['all'].

names.description: [optional] A list of network Names. Supported only for MX 19.1 and above. The order of items matches the order of IDs.

ids.description: [optional] A list of network IDs.

network.description: [optional] A list of network Names and IDs that will connect with this peer. Supported only for MX 19.1 and above.

isRouteBased.description: [optional] If true, the VPN peer is route-based. If not included, the default is false. Supported only for MX 19.1 and above.

ipVersion.description: The IP version of the neighbor

remoteAsNumber.description: Remote ASN of the neighbor. The remote ASN must be an integer between 1 and 4294967295.

ebgpHoldTimer.description: The eBGP hold timer in seconds for each neighbor. The eBGP hold timer must be an integer between 12 and 240.

ebgpMultihop.description: Configure this if the neighbor is not adjacent. The eBGP multi-hop must be an integer between 1 and 255.

enabled.description: Whether BGP TTL security is enabled. Supported only for MX 26.2 and above

ttlSecurity.description: Settings for BGP TTL security to protect BGP peering sessions from forged IP attacks. Supported only for MX 26.2 and above

password.description: Password to configure MD5 authentication between BGP peers. Supported only for MX 26.2 and above

authentication.description: Authentication settings between BGP peers. Supported only for MX 26.2 and above

allowTransit.description: Whether the appliance will advertise routes learned from other Autonomous Systems. Supported only for MX 26.2 and above

receiveLimit.description: Maximum number of prefixes accepted from the remote peer. Must be an integer between 0 and 2147483647. Supported only for MX 26.2 and above

enabled.description: Whether explicit outbound routes are advertised to the eBGP neighbor. Supported only for MX 26.2 and above

explicitOutboundRouteAdvertisement.description: Settings for explicit outbound route advertisement to an eBGP neighbor

out.description: Filters routes advertised to an eBGP neighbor. Each entry must be an IPv4 CIDR string. Supported only for MX 26.2 and above

filter.description: Filters routes for an eBGP neighbor.

filterIn.description: Filters routes received from an eBGP neighbor. Each entry must be an IPv4 CIDR string. Supported only for MX 26.2 and above

communityOut.description: List of BGP communities tagged to the routes advertised to an eBGP neighbor. Supported only for MX 26.2 and above

pathPrepend.description: Prepends the AS_PATH BGP Attribute associated with routes received from the remote peer. Configurable value of ASNs to prepend. Length of the array may not exceed 10, and each ASN in the array must be an integer between 1 and 4294967295. AS_PATH is 4th in the decision tree when identical routes from multiple peers exist.

multiExitDiscriminator.description: Configures the local metric associated with routes received from the remote peer. Routes from peers with lower metrics are will be preferred. Must be an integer between 0 and 4294967295. MED is 6th in the decision tree when identical routes from multiple peers exist.

weight.description: Configures the local metric associated with routes received from the remote peer. Routes from peers with lower metrics are will be preferred. Must be an integer between 0 and 4294967295. MED is 6th in the decision tree when identical routes from multiple peers exist.

ebgpNeighbor.description: [optional] The BGP neighbor configuration for the VPN peer. Supported only for MX 19.1 and above.

id.description: ID of the ECMP uplink configuration

wan.description: The WAN uplink associated with this ECMP configuration.

privateSubnets.description: The private subnets associated with this ECMP uplink configuration.

ebgpNeighbor.description: [optional] The eBGP neighbor configuration associated with this ECMP uplink configuration.

ecmpUplinkConfigs.description: [optional] The ECMP per-uplink BGP-over-IPsec configuration for the VPN peer.

priorityInGroup.description: [optional] Represents the order of peer inside a group.

number.description: [optional] Represents the ordering of primary and backup tunnels group. primary and backup tunnels are grouped by this number. Peers containing same group number belongs to same group.

Return a page of event-log rows for the organization, newest first.
The result set is paginated using an opaque cursor; pass the value of
`nextCursor` from the previous response back as `startingAfter` to
continue. All filter parameters are optional; multi-value filters
(triggerTypes, outcomes, entityTypes, entityIds, cloudProviders,
events, integrationIds, accountIds, vpcIds, siteIds, subnetIds,
deprecated networkIds,
regionNames, userIds, userEmails, groupIds) accept repeated query
parameters.

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: Organization ID

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on event_time (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on event_time (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: triggerType
outcome
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more outcome values (repeatable). Allowed values:
`information`, `warning`, `error`. Validated server-side; unknown
values produce 400.

parameters.name: entityType
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more entity_type values (repeatable). Allowed values:
`integration`, `account`, `vpc`, `site`, `subnet`, and the deprecated
compatibility value `network`. `vpc` and `site` are translated to the
existing persisted `network` entity type by the gateway. Validated
server-side; unknown values produce 400.

parameters.name: entityId
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more entity_id values (repeatable). The
`entity_id` column is the denormalised primary-subject id and is
indexed independently of the per-type *_id columns, so this
filter is the cross-type point lookup.

parameters.name: cloudProvider
event
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more event headline values (repeatable). The
`event` field is a producer-supplied short summary of what
happened (e.g. `Subnet discovered`, `Permissions denied`).
Matching is exact and case-sensitive; the empty string is never
offered as a facet value, so passing it as a chip just resolves
to "no rows".

parameters.name: integrationId
parameters.description: Filter by one or more integration ids (repeatable).

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: Filter by one or more account ids (repeatable).

parameters.name: vpcId
parameters.description: Filter by one or more cloud VPC ids (repeatable).

parameters.name: siteId
parameters.description: Filter by one or more Site ids (repeatable).

parameters.name: subnetId
parameters.description: Filter by one or more subnet ids (repeatable).

parameters.name: regionId
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more region UUIDs (repeatable). Backed by a
bloom-filter skip index on `region_id`, so this is the cheap
cross-region cardinality lookup the UI's region chip emits.

parameters.name: regionName
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more cloud-provider region display names
(repeatable). Useful when the caller only knows the region by
its display string (e.g. `us-east-1`) and not the UUID.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Filter by one or more user_id values (repeatable, opaque IdP subject).

parameters.name: userEmail
parameters.description: Filter by one or more user_email values (repeatable).

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description:
Filter by one or more group_id values (repeatable). Producer-
supplied correlation id; lets the UI collapse events that belong
to the same logical action.

parameters.description: A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.

receivedAt.description: When the ingestor consumer wrote the row.

traceId.description:
Optional W3C Trace Context trace identifier (typically a 32-char
hex). Empty / absent when the producer is not wired into a
tracer. Carried end-to-end so support engineers can correlate an
event with the matching trace in Kibana / Grafana; not currently
rendered as a column on the UI.

triggerType.description:
Closed enum: `user_action`, `system_action`. Documented as a
free-form string here to avoid generator-level enum
deduplication clashing with similarly shaped enums elsewhere
in the spec; the server only emits these two values.

outcome.description:
Closed enum: `information`, `warning`, `error`. Documented as a
free-form string here to avoid generator-level enum deduplication
clashing with similarly shaped enums elsewhere in the spec; the
server only emits these three values.

entityType.description:
Closed persisted enum: `integration`, `account`, `network`, `subnet`.
Network-backed events continue to return `network` for backward
compatibility; use `resourceType` to distinguish a VPC from a Site.
Documented as a free-form string here to avoid generator-level
enum deduplication clashing with similar enums elsewhere in the
spec; the server only emits the values listed above.

resourceType.description:
Preferred resource family for a network entity: `vpc` or `site`.
Omitted for non-network entities and rows whose provider family is
unavailable. This field is additive; `entityType` remains `network`.

entityId.description:
Denormalised primary-subject id (string form of whichever *_id
matches `entityType`). Plain string so future non-UUID entity
types fit.

entityName.description: Snapshotted display name of the primary subject at write time.

cloudProvider.description:
Closed enum: `aws`, `azure`, `gcp`, `meraki`. Documented as a
free-form string here to avoid generator-level enum
deduplication; the server only emits these four values.
Optional - the field is omitted from the response when the
producer did not attribute the event to a specific cloud
provider (e.g. provider-agnostic platform events). UI must
render an em-dash fallback for missing values.

integrationId.description: Optional. Empty when the event is not scoped to an integration.

vpcId.description: Cloud VPC ID. Omitted for Site and non-network events.

vpcName.description: Cloud VPC display name. Omitted for Site and non-network events.

siteId.description: Site ID. Omitted for VPC and non-network events.

siteName.description: Site display name. Omitted for VPC and non-network events.

regionId.description:
Stable identifier for the cloud-provider region the event
happened in. Optional - empty when the producer does not
maintain a region catalog.

regionName.description:
Cloud-provider region display name (e.g. `us-east-1`). Tracks
1:1 with `regionId` and is the snapshotted display value.
Optional.

userId.description:
Opaque actor identifier (e.g. an Okta `sub`). Optional; empty
for `triggerType=system_action`.

userName.description: Display name of the actor. Optional.

groupId.description:
Producer-supplied grouping/correlation id (e.g. a batch
operation id) so the UI can collapse events that belong to the
same logical action. Optional.

event.description:
Short human-facing summary (typically 1-2 words, e.g.
"Tunnel down", "Connection modified") rendered as its own
column in the UI to the left of `details`. Always present;
the empty string indicates the producer did not ship a
summary and the UI renders an em-dash fallback.

details.description: Human-facing event description rendered in the UI.

payload.description:
Raw producer payload (typically JSON) attached to the event.
Optional. Empty / omitted when the producer did not ship a payload.
Returned as a string so the wire format stays opaque to consumers
and large payloads do not bloat schema validation.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; empty when no more rows.

name.description:
Dimension name. One of `trigger_type`, `outcome`, `entity_type`,
`cloud_provider`, `event`, `integration`, `account`, `vpc`, `site`,
`subnet`, `entity`, `region`, `user`, and deprecated `network`.
The `entity` dimension is
the cross-type "(entity_id, entity_name)" pair: it aggregates
events regardless of `entity_type` so the UI can power a single
"Entity" multi-select that mirrors the `entityId` filter. The
`event` dimension is the producer-supplied short headline; its
empty-string bucket is suppressed so the dropdown only offers
meaningful selections.

value.description:
For low-cardinality dimensions (trigger_type, outcome,
entity_type, cloud_provider) this is the column value. For
id+name pair dimensions (integration, account, vpc, site,
subnet, region, and deprecated network) this is the UUID string. For the entity
dimension this is the denormalised primary-subject id (the
same `entityId` shape returned on event rows). For the user
dimension this is the email.

label.description:
Human-readable label rendered in the UI. Equals `value` for
low-cardinality dimensions; the snapshotted name for pair
dimensions (e.g. region_name for the region dim, entity_name
for the entity dim); the user's display name (or email when
blank) for the user dimension.

value.description: VLAN identifier. Can be either a numeric VLAN ID (e.g., '123') or a VLAN name (e.g., 'Guest_Network'). Must match an existing VLAN configured on the network.

vlan.description: VLAN assignment for network segmentation. Allows dynamic assignment of clients to specific VLANs based on authentication conditions for network isolation and access control.

value.description: Adaptive Policy name. Must reference an existing Adaptive Policy configured in the organization (e.g., 'Sample_Adaptive_Policy'). Retrieved from the urn:authzProfile dictionary.

adaptivePolicy.description: Cisco Adaptive Policy (formerly TrustSec SGT) assignment. Enables software-defined segmentation by assigning security group tags to clients for micro-segmentation and policy enforcement across the network infrastructure.

value.description: Voice Domain enabled flag. Boolean value as string: 'true' to enable voice domain prioritization, 'false' to disable. When true, client traffic receives voice-class QoS treatment.

voiceDomain.description: Voice domain classification for Quality of Service (QoS) prioritization. When enabled, marks client traffic for voice-optimized handling with higher priority queuing and reduced latency.

value.description: Group Policy name. Must reference an existing Group Policy configured on the associated network(s) (e.g., 'Sample_Group_Policy'). Retrieved from the urn:meraki:group-policy dictionary and filtered by network IDs.

groupPolicy.description: Meraki Group Policy assignment for comprehensive policy enforcement. Applies network-specific policies including bandwidth limits, firewall rules, traffic shaping, content filtering, and application-level controls.

value.description: Masked IPSK value. Responses do not expose the configured passphrase.

type.description: IPSK value type. Specifies how the value should be interpreted.

isMasked.description: True when the IPSK is configured but intentionally masked in the response.

mode.description: Per-client Identity Pre-Shared Key (iPSK) mode controls key source and fallback behavior. One of: clientIpskOnly (Use only the per-client Identity Pre-Shared Key (iPSK) passphrase assigned to the client. The authorization profile default IPSK is not used.), clientIpskWithDefaultFallback (Prefer the per-client Identity Pre-Shared Key (iPSK) passphrase when the client has one configured; otherwise fall back to the authorization profile default IPSK.), overrideClientIpsk (Use the authorization profile default Identity Pre-Shared Key (iPSK) and override any per-client iPSK passphrase.). Returned on GET when mode is configured.

ipsk.description: Identity Pre-Shared Key (IPSK) used by node during client device association. Responses return a masked marker instead of the plaintext IPSK.

authorizationProfile.description: Authorization profile associated with the rule

rules.description: Rules associated to an authorization policy

hasOutdatedCondition.description: True if any of the condition contains invalid/outdated attribute values

conditionTags.description: Summary of the conditions of rules

get.description: Get point-in-time overview statistics for buildings, floors, maps, and wireless device placement. Counts are computed when requested from current Dashboard data for networks the caller can access. If networkIds is omitted, counts include all accessible networks in the organization. If networkIds is provided, counts include only exact network ID matches the caller can access. Buildings, floors, maps, and devices are separate count categories and should not be summed together. Map counts include the total and 2D map count. Device counts are partitioned by placement state. Percentages are shares of each grouping's total and are rounded to two decimal places.

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: Organization ID

parameters.name: networkIds
parameters.description: Optional parameter to filter statistics by one or more network IDs. This filter uses multiple exact matches. Maximum 100 network IDs.

total.description: Total number of buildings matching the network filter. Minimum 0; no static maximum.

buildings.description: Building counts for matching networks. Buildings are counted when directly assigned to a matching network or when tied to a matching network locale.

total.description: Total number of floor maps attached to matching networks. Minimum 0; no static maximum.
Total number of uploaded floor maps attached to matching networks. Minimum 0; no static maximum.

dimension.description: Map dimension. 2D maps do not have a 3D model.

total.description: Total number of maps in this dimension. Minimum 0; no static maximum.

percentage.description: Percentage of maps.total represented by this dimension. Range 0 to 100.

byDimension.description: Map counts grouped by map dimension. The entry reports 2D maps. Percentages are shares of maps.total.

maps.description: Map counts for matching networks. total is the number of uploaded floor maps attached to matching networks. byDimension includes the 2D map count.

total.description: Total number of wireless devices in matching networks. Minimum 0; no static maximum.

status.description: Device placement state. Placed devices have at least one floor plan placement; unplaced devices do not.

count.description: Total number of devices in this placement state. Minimum 0; no static maximum.

percentage.description: Percentage of devices.total represented by this placement state. Range 0 to 100.

total.description: Total devices and percentage for this placement state.

byPlacement.description: Device counts grouped by placement state. The entries always include placed and unplaced. Percentages are shares of devices.total.

devices.description: Wireless device placement counts for matching networks. byPlacement partitions total into placed and unplaced devices.

counts.description: Point-in-time counts for matching networks. Buildings, floors, maps, and devices are separate categories and should not be summed together.

get.description: Returns the total PoE power draw for all switch ports in the organization over the requested timespan (by default the last 24 hours). draw.description: The PoE power draw in watts for all switch ports in the organization for the given interval.

get.description: Returns the counts of all active ports for the requested timespan, grouped by speed. An active port is a port that at any point during the timeframe is observed to be connected to a responsive device and isn't configured to be disabled. For a port that is observed at multiple speeds during the timeframe, it will be counted at the highest speed observed. The number of inactive ports, and the total number of ports are also provided. Only ports on switches online during the timeframe will be represented and a port is only guaranteed to be present if its switch was online for at least 6 hours of the timeframe.

get.description:
Return deduplicated per-model transmit power maximums and antenna gain for the organization. Each item represents one unique access point model. Items have no independent lifecycle or identifier beyond the model field; each model value is unique within the collection and serves as the natural key. This data is derived from hardware capabilities and regulatory maximums, not user-configurable settings; it virtually never changes. When networkIds[] is provided, the population is restricted to models deployed in those networks. Because capabilities are model-intrinsic (identical for the same model regardless of which network it appears in), network metadata is intentionally omitted from the response; the filter only narrows which deployed models are included. Clients that need to know which networks deploy a specific model should use the device inventory endpoints. The errors array in error responses contains at most 1 element. 

**Error responses:** 400 Bad Request — returned when a query parameter is malformed or out of range (e.g. invalid band value, perPage < 3 or > 200). Body: { "errors": ["radioBands[] must be one of: 2.4, 5, 6"] }. 403 Forbidden — returned when the API key lacks the required wireless:config:read OAuth scope, or when the caller has no RBAC wireless_read or network_admin role on any wireless network in the organization. 404 Not Found — returned when the organization ID does not exist. 429 Too Many Requests — the Retry-After response header contains the number of seconds the client must wait before retrying. 

**Feature gating (G1):** The radio-power-constraints-api feature flag is evaluated once per request using the first eligible network as a representative sample. This is intentional organization-level gating: the flag controls API rollout at the org level, not per-network availability. When disabled, the endpoint returns an empty result. 

**Pagination strategy (F4):** Models are collected from all eligible networks, deduplicated by model name, and sorted alphabetically. The startingAfter cursor is a model name (uppercase). Malformed startingAfter values return 400. 

**Data strategy (F4):** Model and radio data is resolved from in-memory constant maps (RADIO_BDF_TX_POWER_LIMIT, RADIOS_MAP, ANTENNA_GAIN_BY_MODEL), not from additional database queries. The only SQL operations are for network scope resolution and feature flag evaluation. 

**Performance budget and targets (F1/F2 – pending validation):** Known AP model catalog is ~200 models. With flat model-level pagination, worst-case response at perPage=200 is ~200 models × 3 radios ≈ 50 KB. GA-promotion targets (not yet measured): p99 latency ≤ 200 ms at default perPage (100); sustained 50 req/s concurrency without error-rate increase. This endpoint is Alpha-gated. Measured worst-case p99 latency, concurrent load results, and a database-versus-serialization timing breakdown must be attached before advancing toward GA.

**Organization-wide scan plan (F2):** The controller loads all wireless-enabled networks in the organization via a single indexed query (node_groups.has_wireless + JOIN wireless_configs, indexed on organization_id). find_each iterates these networks with batched SQL (1000 per batch). For each network, model and radio data is resolved from in-memory constant maps — no additional SQL per network. Total SQL: 1 scope query + 1 feature-flag check + O(N/1000) batched network loads, where N is the number of wireless networks in the org. Worst-case N for large orgs is ~1000 networks, yielding ~3 SQL queries. Serialization is O(M) where M is the deduplicated model count (~200 max). Pagination bounds the serialized output but not the network scan; this is acceptable because the scan cost is SQL-light (constant maps, no per-network queries) and bounded by org size.
